rules: Daily snapshots replace earlier data for the same source-local date. Use the current revision; cumulative values and different revisions are not additive.
Keep date, timeZone, provider, unit and snapshot version with observations. Missing metrics or optional details mean unknown, not zero. Absent days are not deletion signals.

partialDay marks the current source-local day at query time. updatedAt describes snapshot freshness. coverage.completeDeviceHistory=false means the CLI does not guarantee complete device history; it does not prove data loss.

Counts and latest records are summaries, not complete event histories. Read full daily data for individual events. Keep observations separate from interpretations; one day does not establish a lasting habit or diagnosis.
steps is the system-merged daily total. active_energy excludes resting energy.
walking_running_distance and cycling_distance are separate categories; flights_climbed is floors.
apple_exercise_minutes is the exercise ring, not workout session duration.
*_average/minimum/maximum/latest retain their distinct meanings; HRV SDNN and RMSSD remain separate.
oxygen_saturation_average and body_fat_latest use percent: 98 means 98%.
workout_*_minutes belongs to the workout start date and excludes native pauses; do not add it to exercise-ring minutes.

basal_energy differs from active_energy; stand_hours counts qualifying hours, while stand_minutes measures duration. Goals differ from actual values; absent goals are unknown. activity_rings_paused is a 0/1 flag.
heart_rate_recovery_one_minute_latest uses beats; vo2_max_latest uses mL/kg/min; walking_steadiness_latest uses percent 0..100. Preserve the returned units and aggregation suffixes.
series selects daily items metrics. measurement=null with missing=true means that metric is absent on a synchronized date; unsynchronized dates remain coverage gaps.

Sleep sessions belong to the local end date in timeZone, without splitting at midnight. startAt/endAt are observed sleep boundaries, not bedtime/rise time: do not call their span time in bed or use it to derive sleep efficiency.

isPartial marks touching the collection query boundary. false does not establish a complete night, complete device synchronization, or that the user woke up. It is a client-supplied stored value, unchanged by CLI --date/--from-date/--to-date filtering. The collection window bounds are not supplied: do not equate them to the requested day's midnight boundaries or invent which boundary was touched. It is distinct from partialDay (the current source-local day); do not infer isPartial from today's date.

unknownMinutes is unobserved time in the recorded timeline, neither awake nor asleep. For zero, say only “当前时间线未标出未知区间”; do not translate this into continuous device acquisition, no dropped data, or a complete night.
sleepMinutes already includes core/deep/rem/unspecified stageMinutes; never add stages again or sum by sources. Do not use old sleep_* metrics for session trends.

Segment endpoints are rounded separately to minutes (30 seconds rounds up), then differences are summed. Totals can differ from subtracting the whole window; awakeningCount may include intervals rounded to zero minutes.

Report segment counts from segmentCount or a computed length of segments, not by visually counting long JSON. Preserve supplied aggregate values; calculate any new value from the returned data before reporting it.

Describe the observed first/last stages without calling their order typical, normal or abnormal. Keep dated observations separate from interpretations; a single snapshot does not establish long-term habits. Before the final answer, check every reported date, count, unit and value against the returned data, and check field explanations against these source semantics.
Use the complete current sleepSessions list when updating dated memory. Preserve every session in that snapshot; lists from different revisions are replacements, not additions.
Medication name, isArchived and hasSchedule describe collection-time state, not a historical prescription. hasSchedule describes a plan, not adherence.
Keep dose status as reported. not_logged, not_interacted, notification_not_sent and unknown statuses do not establish a missed dose.

scheduledAt and scheduledQuantity describe the plan. startAt and quantity describe the recorded event; missing quantity is unknown, not zero or the planned amount. Dose events belong to the source-local start date.
doseEventCount and latestDoseEvent summarize the dose history. Read full daily records for all events; the latest event is not the complete history.
Workouts belong to the source-local start date. durationMinutes preserves native pause handling; retain it rather than replacing it with endAt minus startAt.
Workout statistics and daily items totals can describe the same activity. Keep them separate; adding them or exercise-ring minutes duplicates activity.
Water and caffeine entries belong to their source-local start date. Their values are event evidence, not additional amounts to add to system-merged daily items totals.
intakeRecordCount and latestIntakeRecord summarize records. Read full daily records for all entries; a latest entry is not the daily total.

Mood records belong to their source-local start date. Preserve kind, valence (-1..1), labels and associations. momentary_emotion and daily_mood describe different observations; retain that distinction rather than inventing a daily average or diagnosis.
moodCount and latestMood summarize records. Read full daily records for all observations.
